idiom_name: node types with a normalized child-list protocol
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: derive every node type from one base that owns the single child-collection protocol (children(), child_nodes, ChildNodes()), have each node's constructor append its children to that collection in a documented order, and never let a node keep a child outside the collection. One generic walker/visitor over the protocol then serves printing, rewriting, serialisation, tree matching and every analysis, while node-specific data stays typed on the concrete node. Choose this normalized form when several passes traverse arbitrary subtrees (external visitors, tree pattern matchers); choose named per-node fields when node-specific operations dominate. Keep the collection read-only after construction and provide exactly one traversal entry point.
code_sketch:
node Add:  children = [left, right]          # each node appends its own children
node If:   children = [cond, then, else]

walk(n):
    visit(n)
    for c in n.children(): walk(c)       # one walker for every node type
pitfalls: Node-specific children kept outside the collection are invisible to every generic pass - a subtree that never gets printed, rewritten or type-checked.
Positional order left undocumented, so different passes disagree about which child plays which role.
A rewritten node that forgets to re-append its children drops that subtree from every later traversal.

Wrong move: add a semantic child to a named field but not the canonical child sequence -> generic visitors silently skip that subtree -> instead construct children once through the factory or constructor and assert a canonical dump reaches every semantic child.

Wrong move: treat tokens, comments, or trivia as ordinary semantic children -> analyses recurse into non-AST payload and child order becomes unstable -> instead expose token/trivia access separately and define the normalized sequence as semantic nodes only.

Wrong move: publish mutable child storage or make callers infer roles solely from indexes -> rewrites can invalidate invariants or analyses can misidentify roles -> instead expose a read-only sequence with documented order and retain typed role fields or accessors.
